body:
samir: FYI ACME's dedicated pool is still returning 429s after their plan bump last night. Support ticket 5482. They say traffic dropped but errors persist. Any ideas?

ops-bot: Notice: automated alert — tenant=acme-prod returned 429s (rate_limit) at 2026-03-16T23:01:12Z

lina: Can you paste a sample request/response and the tenant id? Also which pool (quiet vs default)?

samir: tenant_id=acme-prod, pool=quiet-pool-3. Sample curl: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` -> `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
Response headers:
`x-rw-rate-remaining: 0`
`x-rw-rate-window: 60`
`x-rw-plan: enterprise-plus`

jesse: Quick hypothesis: when they migrated plans the quota rows were updated but the dedicated routing/cache layer kept an in-memory per-tenant ratewindow that wasn't invalidated. That makes the tenant look like it's still at 0 remaining until the window expires.

irene: We saw something similar last month with the cooldown unit mismatch (mins vs secs). Can someone check `quota_config` for acme-prod? SQL I ran: `select tenant, units, window_secs from tenant_quota where tenant='acme-prod';`

samir: Paste from prod read replica:
`acme-prod | 10000 | 3600`
Looks sane.

jesse: OK. Next: check `quota_cache_version` vs DB `quota_version`. Run: `redis-cli GET quota:acme-prod:version` and `select quota_version from tenant_quota where tenant='acme-prod';`

lina: I ran that — redis has `v12`, DB shows `v13`. So cache is stale.

jesse: There's the problem. The quota upsert on plan change failed to publish an invalidation event to the routing tier because the publisher timed out. The routing tier uses the cached version and treats it as still at the old usage counters.

samir: What's the immediate patch? Can we flush only that tenant cache? Don't want to flush whole pool.

jesse: Hotfix: POST to internal admin endpoint: `POST /admin/quotas/flush` body `{ "tenant": "acme-prod" }` — hits routing tier and invalidates cache for that tenant. I just ran it in staging and it cleared the cache and requests started succeeding.

lina: Steps to reproduce for ops runbook:
1. Set tenant quota in DB (increment version).
2. Simulate publisher timeout (kill publisher pod) so event doesn't reach routing.
3. Send requests until routing still uses cached version -> expect persistent 429s.

jesse: Longer-term fix: make quota writer retry publish and fall back to synchronous invalidation for Dedicated pools, and add a health metric `quota_invalidation_lag`. I'll open PR after I verify no side effects.

irene: For now I executed the tenant-specific flush in prod. Verified with curl: got `200` and `x-rw-rate-remaining: 9999`. Support notified ACME.

samir: Thanks. Support confirmed errors stopped ~4m after the flush. Ticket updated.

lina: Action items:
- jesse: PR for publisher retries + metric (P0 for Dedicated)
- infra: add alert for `quota_invalidation_lag > 30s`
- support: follow up with customer and document workaround in KB

ops-bot: NOTE: deploy event — quota-publisher v2.1.3 rolled out to prod at 2026-03-17T00:12:00Z (contains retry loop) :rocket:

samir: Closing thread once PR merged and KB published. :thumbsup:
